data.hook: Metalbone attack in an oversize diamond, with a spin-gripping face and a softer core.
why: Oversize diamond lifts the sweet spot for big, clean smashes
6K carbon face and frame with the Octagonal Structure for stiffness and durability
Spin Blade textured surface grips the ball for heavy spin
Soft Performance EVA core keeps vibration down in long sessions
Power balance designed for advanced, attacking players
data.playStyle: Aggressive players who live at the net and want to finish points with bandejas, viboras and flat smashes.
data.summary: The Metalbone Carbon 3.3 brings adidas's flagship attacking shape to a 6K carbon build. The oversize diamond and power balance give explosive smashes, the Spin Blade surface adds bite, and the Soft Performance EVA core keeps it comfortable.
data.description:
This is a high-performance racket for advanced players who want to dictate from the net. The oversize diamond head raises the sweet spot, so contact up high on smashes and decisive volleys pays off with maximum power.

A 6K carbon frame and face with adidas's Octagonal Structure keep the racket stiff and durable, and perimeter reinforcements help it stand up to hard play. The soft, low-density EVA core reduces arm fatigue, while the new Spin Blade relief helps you load the ball with spin.

tech.name: Octagonal Structure
tech.text: Octagonal-section tubular frame for extra rigidity at impact.

tech.name: Structural Reinforcement
tech.text: Perimeter reinforcements that resist the stress of hard matches.

tech.name: Soft Performance
tech.text: Low-density EVA rubber for good ball reaction and comfort.

tech.name: Spin Blade
tech.text: Raised face texture that adds control and spin.

tech.name: Carbon Fiber 6K
tech.text: Carbon weave that keeps the build light while reinforcing key points.

tech.name: Metalbone Protector Tape
tech.text: Light, durable 3M edge protector made for Metalbone rackets.

faq.a: Yes. It is a unisex racket.

data.clubTake: Brand new, unused. Metalbone power at a friendlier price point than the HRD and Ale Galán editions.
